intent: Stack a run of item rows into one spaced column exposed as a list.
typical_uses: The rows of one collection, such as a file list or a notification feed

dont_use_when.situation: Tabular data read across rows and columns
A set of options the user picks exactly one of

invariants.text: ItemGroup renders a div with role="list", which a consumer's own `role` replaces; Item sets no role of its own and ItemSeparator carries the primitive's role="separator", so the list's rows are exposed as list items only when each Item is given role="listitem".
The group is a full-width flex column spaced var(--space-4) apart; the gap becomes var(--space-3) when any Item inside it has `size="sm"`, and var(--space-2) when any has `size="xs"`.

anti_patterns.dont: Set a row size through a className and expect the group's gap to follow
anti_patterns.do_instead: Set `size` on each Item; the gap reads the size class Item emits from its own `size`, not a consumer class

a11y.by: item.test.tsx asserts the group's role="list", while item.tsx gives Item no role and ItemSeparator keeps the primitive's role="separator", so a group built as item.md shows exposes a list whose children are not list items, the role WAI-ARIA requires a list to own

good.title: A run of rows exposed as list items

bad.title: Rows wrapped in a list element of their own
bad.why: The group is already the list; a nested ul puts a second list inside it, and the rows are no longer the group's own children, so its column gap does not space them.
